post.description: Creates a new asset and places it in the specified asset category. Requires "Assets" create permission. Returns 422 if an asset with the same name, order code, serial number, reference name, client, and location already exists in the category. If `parentAssetId` is provided, the parent asset must exist and must have `allowSubAssets` enabled — otherwise a 422 is returned. If `dateCreated` is omitted, it defaults to the current date. Default custom fields are created for the new asset from any applicable custom field templates — global templates, plus templates scoped to the asset types in `assetTypeIds`.

orderCode.description: The order code for the asset.

quantity.description: Quantity of the asset. Defaults to 1 if not provided.

referenceName.description: A short reference name for the asset.

patch.description:
Partially updates an existing asset by its unique identifier. Only the fields included in the request body are updated — omitted fields are left unchanged. Requires "Assets" edit permission.
If `clientId` or `locationId` changes, a record is written to the asset move-history table.
If `assetTypeIds` is provided, the full set of asset-type links for the asset is replaced (existing links not in the array are removed). Custom fields are synced to match: empty custom fields scoped to an asset type that's no longer linked are removed, and custom fields for newly-linked asset types (plus any global templates) are created. Custom fields that already have a value are never removed, even if their asset type is unlinked.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the asset (base-encoded).
parameters.name: assetId

schema.description: Partial update payload for an asset. All fields are optional. Only provided fields are written to the database.

assetTypeIds.description: Full replacement list of asset-type identifiers (base-encoded). Existing links not in this list are removed.

clientId.description: Base-encoded client or business unit identifier. The server first resolves the value against the client table; if not found, it falls back to the business unit table.

lastChecked.description: Pass false to clear the lastChecked value.

locationId.description: Base-encoded location identifier. Pass empty string to clear.

patch.description:
Performs a partial update to a client record, modifying only the specified fields.
Requires "Clients" edit permission.

Notes:
- All request body fields are optional — only provided fields will be updated.
- Passing an empty string for `abn`, `website`, `phone`, `fax`, `mobile`, `email`, `termsNote`, or `clientMessage` will clear those fields.
- `name` cannot be cleared; an empty string will be rejected by input validation.
- `clientMessage` is stored separately and supports both create and delete via this endpoint.
- `status` must be either `active` or `archived`.
- `transactionTerms.id` must be an encoded ID of a non-archived transaction term.
- `parentId` must be an encoded ID of an existing client, or omit to leave unchanged. Pass an empty string to remove the parent relationship.
- `contactId` accepts an encoded user ID to set as the primary contact/manager.
- `phone`, `fax`, `mobile`, and `email` update the contact record of the client's primary contact. If `contactId` is also provided in the same request, the contact record of the newly assigned contact is updated. If no `contactId` is provided, the existing primary contact's record is updated.
- `address` and `mailAddress` each accept a partial address object; only provided sub-fields are updated.

post.description:
Creates a new contact for the specified client and returns the created
record. A client contact is stored as a user linked to the client's org,
with its access type fixed to `PERMISSION_GROUPS`. Requires both "Clients"
and "Contacts" create permission.

Notes:
- `givenName`, `familyName`, and `email` are required (the keys must be present in the body).
- `givenName` and `familyName` must be at least 2 characters.
- `email` must be a valid email address when a non-empty value is supplied. Field-level validation reports this field as `emailaddress`.
- Passing an empty string for `email` is accepted and stored as null (the contact is still created).
- `username` is auto-generated and `accessType` is always `PERMISSION_GROUPS`; neither can be set via this endpoint.
- Within `address`, `state` and `country` are stored as free text and normalised to uppercase in the response.
- `address` is optional, but when supplied it must be complete: `addressLine`, `suburb`, `state`, `country` and `postcode` are all required, otherwise a 400 is returned.
- Creating a contact whose given name and surname match an existing (including archived) user in the company returns 409.

get.summary: List custom fields for a zone and entity

patch.description: Updates the values of existing custom fields for a given zone and entity ID. Only fields whose value rows already exist on the entity can be updated — the endpoint never creates new custom field rows. Required-field completeness is enforced per request: every applicable custom field that is required on creation (or required on completion, once the entity is completed) must be included in the request unless it already holds a stored value; the 400 error lists the missing fields by id and name. Validation is atomic: if any submitted field fails validation (unknown template, invalid option, exceeding the template's configured max length, missing required value, or no existing field row), the entire request fails with a 400 and no values are written. An archived template stays updatable while the record still carries a live value row for it — whether a field is available on a record is decided by the record's own value row, not the template's archived flag. For the TASKS and TASK_ASSETS zones the set of available templates depends on the site setting "Use individual Custom Fields for each Business Unit": when it is enabled, only templates belonging to the task's business unit are accepted; a template from another business unit is rejected as not available for the record. Business-unit access is enforced on writes for BU-scoped zones (TASKS, TASK_ASSETS, WORK_ORDERS, PROJECTS, PURCHASE_ORDERS) — updating a record owned by a business unit the caller cannot access is refused. For TASK_ASSETS, custom fields are not available while the parent task is in the Quote status.

parameters.name: zone

parameters.description: The encoded identifier for the entity in the specified zone.

value.description: The value to store. Option-based types (RADIO/SELECT/CHECKBOX/MULTISELECT) are validated against the template's options; CHECKBOX accepts yes/no (or the stored 1/0 as returned by GET, so a read value can be resubmitted unchanged). For NON-required fields, omitting this property (or sending null or an empty string) deliberately clears the stored value. Required fields never accept a blank value — omitting/blanking one returns a 400.

Resolves the default email recipient fields (to, cc, bcc) for an invoice's client, delegating to the org-level email defaults shared with the billing portal (Layout_Email_Default / Email_Default).

Resolution is scoped to the Invoices zone and the subzone matching the invoice's own type (e.g. PART_INVOICES for a Part Invoice), and follows this hierarchy: 1. Client-level email default 2. Owning Business Unit email default 3. Top-level (controlling org) email default 4. System Default: falls back to the invoice client's assigned Manager
   email for 'to' only


If the effective 'to' setting has no usable email address (e.g. no manager is assigned to the client and no other default is configured), 'to' is returned with an empty email rather than the request failing. Empty 'cc' or 'bcc' values are valid.

Returns a paginated list of an invoice's line items.

Feature Access controls line item pricing, using Labour Visibility for `LABOUR` items and Material and Expense Visibility for all other items. Fields the user can't see are null:
- `cost` and `markup` need "Show Cost" or "Show All".
- `sell` needs "Show Sell" or "Show All" ("Show Charge" or "Show All" for labour).
- `discount` and `totalEx` need any option except "Show No Pricing".

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of projects visible to the authenticated user's controlling organisation. Filter by business unit and status. Each item includes the owning business unit, client, project type, status, substatus, manager and dates.
Requires standard login authentication and "Projects" list permission. The "owner" property is omitted when the user does not have the Projects "Owner" field view permission, and the businessUnitId filter requires that same permission.
When the user's permission group has the Projects "Tasks Assigned to User" filter enabled, the list only includes projects that have at least one task currently assigned to the user, and "count" reports the size of that restricted set.

patch.description:
Partially updates a project. Only the fields present in the request body are changed - omitted fields keep their current value.
The 'projectTypeId', 'locationId' and 'managerId' fields each accept either an encoded identifier or the literal string "NULL" to clear the value (e.g. sending managerId "NULL" clears the project's manager to none).
Cross-field rules are validated against the EFFECTIVE values (the new value where supplied, otherwise the project's current one): the contact must be a contactable user of the client, a client-owned location must belong to the client, and the end date cannot be before the start date. Changing 'clientId' therefore requires a compatible 'contactId' (and 'locationId' where set) in the same request.
If 'businessUnitId' is provided it is a scope check only - the project must belong to that business unit or the request fails with 404; it does NOT move the project to another business unit. When omitted, the project's owning business unit is used.
Requires standard login authentication and "Projects" edit permission.

post.description:
Creates a quote and returns it. Pass `taskId` to quote an existing task that doesn't already have a quote, or omit it and pass `businessUnitId`, `clientId`, `taskTypeId` and `quoteName` to create the task as well. The estimator defaults to the current user and the quote type to the organisation default.

Feature Access controls the pricing in `counts`. Fields the user can't see are omitted:
- `total`, `tax`, `markup`, `labourMarkup` and `materialMarkup` need Quote Pricing Visibility "Overall Totals" or "All".
- `materials` needs Material and Expense Visibility "Show Sell" or "Show All".
- `labour` needs Labour Visibility "Show Charge" or "Show All".

Requires the `quotes:create` permission and access to the task's business unit. Also requires `tasks:create` when `taskId` is omitted, and `users:list` to set another user as `estimatorId`.

inline_task_complete.summary: Inline-task mode - all task and quote fields

value.description: Full installation of split system AC unit in server room

inline_task_minimal.summary: Inline-task mode - creates task and quote (required fields only)

businessUnitId.description: Inline-task mode only. The encoded identifier of the owning business unit for the task that will be created alongside the quote. Required when `taskId` is not supplied.

clientId.description: Inline-task mode only. The encoded identifier of the client for the task that will be created alongside the quote. Required when `taskId` is not supplied.

description.description: Inline-task mode only. A detailed description of the task that will be created.

dueDate.description: Inline-task mode only. The due date for the task in ISO date format. Defaults to the current date if omitted.

enteredBy.description: Inline-task mode only. The name of the person who entered the task. Defaults to the authenticated user's username (truncated to 25 characters) when omitted.

estimatorId.description: The unique identifier of the user to assign as the estimator. Defaults to the current user if not provided. Requires "Users" list permission when setting a different user.

isTaxInclusive.description: Whether the quote should be tax inclusive. Defaults to false if not provided.

locationId.description: Inline-task mode only. The encoded identifier of the location for the task. Must belong to the provided client. If omitted, the client's address is used.

priorityId.description: Inline-task mode only. The encoded identifier of the task priority.

quoteName.description: Inline-task mode only. The name/title of the task that will be created. Required when `taskId` is not supplied.

quoteType.description: The type of quote to create. If omitted, the default Quote Type configured in Site Admin for the organisation is used, which may be SIMPLE or DETAILED.

reportedByUserId.description: Inline-task mode only. The encoded identifier of the user who reported the new task. When supplied and the task's client is a client, this must be one of that client's contacts; when the client is a business unit, it must be a member of that business unit. Defaults to the authenticated user when omitted.

taskId.description: The unique identifier of the task to create a quote for. The task must not already have an existing quote. When omitted, the inline-task fields become required and a new task is created behind the scenes.

taskTypeId.description: Inline-task mode only. The encoded identifier of the task type. Required when `taskId` is not supplied.

Returns a single quote, including `counts` of its related items and totals.

Feature Access controls the pricing in `counts`. Fields the user can't see are omitted:
- `total`, `tax`, `markup`, `labourMarkup` and `materialMarkup` need Quote Pricing Visibility "Overall Totals" or "All".
- `materials` needs Material and Expense Visibility "Show Sell" or "Show All".

The caller must have access to the quote's business unit, otherwise 403.

Requires the `quotes:view` permission. When the `quotes:filter:created-by-user:view` filter applies, quotes whose task the user didn't report return 403. When the `quotes:filter:estimated-by-user:view` filter applies, quotes the user isn't the estimator of return 403. When both apply, the user must have reported the task or be the estimator.

post.description: Performs a bulk create operation to register multiple quote line items in a single transaction. This action returns the count of inserted line items and their identifiers. The quote must have a status of In Progress. If the quote type is DETAILED, every line item must include a `takeoffId` belonging to that quote - requests without one are rejected with a 422 response, a takeoffId that does not exist on the quote is rejected with a 400 response, and in both cases no line items are created. LABOUR line items support a work type (`workTypeId`) and total hours (`unitLabHours`); their cost, markup, name, and labour tracking centre default from the work type and tracking centre diagram when omitted, and their sell price is derived as costEx x (1 + markup/100) unless a non-zero `unitSell` is provided - matching the quote worksheet, which treats a zero sell with a non-zero cost as "derive from cost and markup". All resources provided in a single request share the same `group_id`, representing a single scheduling event across multiple resources.

**Required fields:**
- `startDateTime`: Local datetime in ISO 8601 format (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss`). Not UTC — do not include a timezone offset or `Z` suffix.

- `businessUnitId`: Override the business unit (defaults to the authenticated user's business unit).

**Permissions required:**

delete.description:
Deletes a calendar schedule record: a task schedule, an ad-hoc event schedule, or a periodic occurrence.

Any schedule returned by `GET /schedules` or `POST /schedules` can be deleted. Two kinds of record are
refused with `422`: a periodic template's baseline schedules, which define the template rather than an
occurrence, and schedule records with no user, asset or crew resource attached. Timesheet entries are not
schedules and return `404`.

- `USER` and `ASSET` schedules: the single schedule record identified by `scheduleId` is deleted. For an
  ad-hoc event with several resources this removes only the targeted resource; the event's other schedules
  are untouched.
- Crew schedules: `POST /schedules` with a `CREW` resource creates one schedule record per crew member and
  returns each as its own `USER` or `ASSET` item. Deleting any one of those records removes the **whole crew
  occurrence** (every member record for that crew, task or event, and start date), mirroring the office
  calendar's "remove crew" action. `X-Affected-Count` reports how many records were removed.
- Periodic occurrences: deleting the last remaining occurrence of a periodic template regenerates the
  template's next occurrence from its baseline at the template's due date, exactly as the office calendar
  does.

Deleting a schedule replicates the data side-effects of removing it from the calendar: removal of queued
reminders (when no other resource remains in the schedule group), Google Calendar removal for synced users,
geofence clean-up, and periodic regeneration. No event message or cancellation email is sent: the
schedule-deleted event message the office calendar triggers is not sent for API deletes.

**Optional query parameters:**
- `businessUnitId`: Override the business unit whose timezone and calendar-sync settings the delete side-effects run under (defaults to the business unit the schedule belongs to).

**Permissions required:**
- `Scheduling` delete permission.
- `Scheduling` delete field permission on Tasks.
- Access to the business unit the schedule belongs to (the caller's own business unit, or one granted through
  the Business Unit access settings). Otherwise `403`.
- Client users are not permitted to access this endpoint.

parameters.description: The encoded identifier of the schedule, as returned by `GET /schedules` or `POST /schedules`.
parameters.name: scheduleId

parameters.description: Optional. Overrides the business unit whose timezone and calendar-sync settings the delete side-effects run under; by default the schedule's own business unit is used. It does not select which schedule is deleted: the schedule is identified by `scheduleId`, and the caller must have access to the business unit that schedule belongs to.
parameters.name: businessUnitId

204.description: Schedule deleted successfully. No content is returned.

X-Affected-Count.description: Number of schedule records deleted. `1` for a USER or ASSET schedule; the number of crew member records for a crew occurrence.

post.description:
Creates a new contact for the specified supplier and returns the created
record. A supplier contact is stored as a user linked to the supplier's org,
with its access type fixed to `PERMISSION_GROUPS`. Requires both "Suppliers"
and "Contacts" create permission.

Notes:
- `givenName`, `familyName`, and `email` are required (the keys must be present in the body).
- `givenName` and `familyName` must be at least 2 characters.
- `email` must be a valid email address when a non-empty value is supplied. Field-level validation reports this field as `emailaddress`.
- Passing an empty string for `email` is accepted and stored as null (the contact is still created).
- `username` is auto-generated and `accessType` is always `PERMISSION_GROUPS`; neither can be set via this endpoint.
- `positionId` is optional; when supplied it must reference an existing position (see `GET /businessunits/{businessUnitId}/settings/positions`) belonging to the controlling org, otherwise a 400 is returned.
- Within `address`, `state` and `country` are stored as free text and normalised to uppercase in the response.
- `address` is optional, but when supplied it must be complete: `addressLine`, `suburb`, `state`, `country` and `postcode` are all required, otherwise a 400 is returned.
- The supplier must not be a contractor; a contractor id returns 404.
- Creating a contact whose given name and surname match an existing (including archived) user in the company returns 409.

post.description:
Uploads a document and attaches it to the specified task. The document is stored in AWS S3 and linked to the task. Supports a JSON body with a base64-encoded `dataUrl` or a raw `base64` string, or a raw binary request body sent with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`. Files up to 250 MB are accepted.
Requires authentication and the "Tasks > Documents and Photos" create permission on the target task.
**Third-party API:** AWS S3 — used for object storage (`PutObject` request with `Content-Type` header and `READ` ACL granted to `AllUsers`).

parameters.description: The encoded identifier of the task to attach the document to.
parameters.name: taskId

parameters.description: The original filename including extension. Required for `application/octet-stream` requests when the `Content-Disposition` header does not supply a filename. Ignored for JSON requests (use the `filename` body field instead).
parameters.name: filename

base64.description: Raw base64-encoded file content. Used when `dataUrl` is not provided. Mutually exclusive with `dataUrl`.

categoryId.description: Optional. The encoded identifier of a folder on this task. Obtain valid values from `GET /tasks/{taskId}/documents/folders`.

comment.description: Optional. A comment to attach to the document link.

dataUrl.description: A base64-encoded data URL representing the file content (e.g. `data:image/jpeg;base64,/9j/4AAQ...`). When provided, mime type and document type are derived from the data URL. Mutually exclusive with `base64`.

description.description: Optional. A description for the document.
description.example: Pre-work site condition

documentFilter.description: Optional. Controls document visibility. Defaults to the task's client / business unit default upload filter.

filename.description: The original filename including extension. Must include a valid file extension. The filename will be normalized: whitespace collapsed to underscores, slashes replaced with hyphens, unsupported characters stripped, and truncated to 255 characters.

imageResolution.description: Optional. Overrides the business unit's configured Default Image Upload Resolution when `useImageUploadResolution` is `true`. `100000` means original size (a 4096 px hard cap still applies). Ignored when `useImageUploadResolution` is absent or `false`.

linkedOrgId.description: Optional. The encoded identifier of the linked org to associate this document with. Defaults to the controlling org.

publicUntilUtc.description: Optional. UTC datetime until which the document is publicly accessible.

useImageUploadResolution.description: Optional. When `true`, the server resizes the image to the business unit's configured Default Image Upload Resolution (typically applied in Field) before storing it.

schema.description: The raw binary file content. The filename must be supplied either via a `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<name>"` header or the `?filename=` query parameter.

Adds a material to a task and returns it.

Feature Access controls material pricing. Fields the user can't see are omitted:
- `cost` needs Material and Expense Visibility "Show Cost" or "Show All".
- `sell` needs "Show Sell" or "Show All".
- `markup` needs "Show All".

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of timesheet entries from `entryDate`. `subZone` picks the type: `TASK_TIMESHEETS` for task labour, `OVERHEAD_TIMESHEETS` for overheads or `EXPENSE_TIMESHEETS` for expenses.

Feature Access controls labour rates. Fields the user can't see are omitted:
- `costRate` needs Labour Visibility "Show Cost" or "Show All".
- `sellRate` needs "Show Charge" or "Show All".

`TASK_TIMESHEETS` requires the `tasks:view` and `tasks:field:labour:view` permissions; `OVERHEAD_TIMESHEETS` and `EXPENSE_TIMESHEETS` require the `timesheets:type:overhead:list` permission. For task labour, a `taskId` blocked by task restrictions returns 403, and when the `tasks:filter:labour-created-by-or-assigned-to-user:view` filter applies, only entries the user is assigned to or created are returned and another user's `userId` returns 403.

parameters.description: The subzone type to filter timesheet entries by. Determines which category of entries to return.
parameters.name: subzone

parameters.description: Filter timesheets on or after this date (inclusive). Format YYYY-MM-DD. Required for all subzone types.
parameters.name: entryDate

parameters.description: Filter timesheets on or before this date (inclusive). Format YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to entryDate if not provided.
parameters.name: endDate

parameters.description: The encoded identifier of the task to filter by. Optional. Applies to TASK_TIMESHEETS (returns 403 if access is restricted, 404 if the task does not exist) and EXPENSE_TIMESHEETS (filters without existence check). Not applicable for OVERHEAD_TIMESHEETS.
parameters.name: taskId

parameters.description: The encoded identifier of the user to filter timesheets for. Optional for all subzone types.
parameters.name: userId

parameters.description: The encoded identifier of the overhead to filter by. Optional. Only applies when subzone is OVERHEAD_TIMESHEETS or EXPENSE_TIMESHEETS. Returns 404 if the overhead does not exist.
parameters.name: overheadId

parameters.description: Filter by the encoded identifier of the work type. Optional.
parameters.name: workTypeId

parameters.description: Filter by the encoded identifier of the tracking centre. Optional.
parameters.name: trackingCentreId

parameters.description: The page number for pagination (default is 1).
parameters.name: page

parameters.description: The number of items per page (default is 30, max is 100).
parameters.name: limit

post.description:
Creates a new line item on an outbound work order.
Requires "Work Orders" edit permission.

Inbound work orders are not supported — the request will be rejected with a 400 error.

The `type` field defaults to `LABOUR` when omitted. `quantityOrdered` defaults to `1` when omitted. `totalEx` is calculated server-side and should not be provided.

`taxCode` is optional — when omitted, or when the provided code is not recognised, the business unit's default tax code is used. If the business unit has no default tax code configured, `GST` at 10% is used. `taxRate` is always resolved server-side from the `taxCode` and is ignored if provided in the request body.

**LABOUR-specific fields** (`hours`, `startDateTime`, `endDateTime`) are only applied when `type` is `LABOUR` (or omitted). `hours` takes priority over the datetime pair. If neither is provided, hours defaults to `0`.

parameters.description: API encoded ID of the work order.
parameters.name: workOrderId

description.description: Description of the line item.
description.example: Supply and install copper pipe

endDateTime.description: User local time.LABOUR line item type only. End datetime of work. Must be after `startDateTime`.

hours.description: LABOUR line item type only. Number of hours worked. Sets both `quantity` and `hours` on the line item. Takes priority over `startDateTime`/`endDateTime`.

partNumber.description: Part number for the line item.

quantityOrdered.description: Quantity ordered. Defaults to `1` when omitted. For `LABOUR` type, use `hours` or `startDateTime`/`endDateTimeUTC` to set quantity instead.

startDateTime.description: User local time.LABOUR line item type only. Start datetime of work. Used with `endDateTime` to calculate decimal hours when `hours` is not provided.

taxCode.description: Tax code to apply to the line item (e.g. `GST`). When omitted, or when the provided code is not recognised, the business unit's default tax code is used. Falls back to `GST` at 10% if the business unit has no tax code configured.

taxRate.description: Ignored — the tax rate is always resolved server-side from the `taxCode`.

trackingCentreId.description: API encoded ID of the tracking centre to assign to the line item. The tracking centre must allow the specified `type`.

type.description: The type of line item. Defaults to `LABOUR` when omitted.
